dedupe_keys.name: satellite monitoring of pipeline rights of way with very high and medium resolution optical imagery

description: This method, presented by Igor Zakharov, Paul Adlakha, Thomas Puestow, Desmond Power, Sherry Warren and Mark Howell at the 22nd Pipeline Technology Conference, uses new optical satellite constellations and largely automated algorithms to monitor oil and gas pipeline rights-of-way, which are usually surveyed from the air or the ground. Coverage: study areas in Canada and the continental US, where encroachment events and changes in surface conditions on or near the right-of-way were detected; very-high-resolution imagery from missions including WorldView-3 and GeoEye-1 was used to estimate population density in high-consequence areas and to detect signs of third-party intervention, and medium-resolution imagery from Landsat-8, Sentinel-2, Planet Labs and RapidEye to find major land cover changes such as flooding and deforestation near corridors. The authors cite wider and more frequent coverage, characterised incidents, fewer false alarms and a growing archive for operators. Format and access: a conference abstract page; the paper and video need free registration. Licence and cost: free after registration; no licence stated. Caveats: the abstract was the part read and the operators are not named. The detections can feed third-party damage and flood hazard exposure layers for pipeline risk models. It relates to the National Pipeline Mapping System and PHMSA incident data in the catalogue.
